objections.claim: The release gate authenticates the tag, verifier closures, and workflow digest only from inside `release.yml`, but the approach never binds the release workflow definition before it begins executing with publication permissions, OIDC, variables, or secrets. GitHub loads a push-triggered workflow from the event’s associated commit/ref, including workflows not merged to the default branch ([GitHub workflow semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflows)); therefore, a tag pushed at an off-main commit can supply a modified `release.yml` that omits every in-workflow ancestry/signature/digest check and exercises privileged release operations before those checks could reject it. Specify a trigger whose workflow definition is platform-selected from protected trusted main (with the release tag passed only as validated data), keep privileged jobs unreachable until that trusted gate succeeds, and add an off-main-tag/malicious-release-workflow regression proving no privileged job starts and no release mutation occurs.
